test_cases.title: backend/.env.example documents JWT_SECRET_KEY with placeholder and comment
test_cases.when: the file is parsed for env var entries
test_cases.then: a JWT_SECRET_KEY line is present with value CHANGE_ME (not a real secret) and is preceded by a comment describing its purpose and production-generation guidance

test_cases.title: backend/.env.example never contains a real JWT secret value
test_cases.given: the repository's backend/.env.example file committed to version control
test_cases.then: its value is exactly the placeholder CHANGE_ME (or empty) and is never a random/production-looking secret string

test_cases.title: docker-compose.yml passes JWT_SECRET_KEY to the backend service via environment
test_cases.then: JWT_SECRET_KEY is listed referencing a host env var (e.g. ${JWT_SECRET_KEY}), never a literal secret, and CORS_ORIGINS is present or confirmed passed through

test_cases.title: docker-compose up starts the backend successfully when JWT_SECRET_KEY is set on the host
test_cases.given: JWT_SECRET_KEY is exported on the host environment before docker-compose up
test_cases.then: the backend container starts successfully and the /api/health endpoint returns 200

test_cases.title: Backend fails fast with a readable error when JWT_SECRET_KEY is missing
test_cases.given: JWT_SECRET_KEY is unset in the backend process environment
test_cases.when: the FastAPI app's on_startup() handler runs
test_cases.then: startup raises an exception with the readable message 'JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable is required' and no raw stack trace is surfaced to logs or clients

test_cases.title: Backend fails fast with a readable error when JWT_SECRET_KEY is an empty string
test_cases.given: JWT_SECRET_KEY is set to an empty string in the backend process environment
test_cases.when: the FastAPI app's on_startup() handler runs
test_cases.then: startup raises the same readable 'JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable is required' error as the unset case

test_cases.title: Backend starts normally and seeds data when JWT_SECRET_KEY is present and non-empty
test_cases.given: JWT_SECRET_KEY is set to a non-empty value in the backend process environment
test_cases.then: on_startup() completes without raising, and existing seed-data behavior is unaffected

test_cases.title: Startup env-var validation adds negligible overhead to container boot time
test_cases.given: the backend container with JWT_SECRET_KEY validation added to on_startup()
test_cases.when: startup time is measured with and without the validation logic
test_cases.then: total added startup latency is well under the 1s budget (target: <10ms added)

test_cases.title: Protected endpoint accepts Authorization header cross-origin under docker-compose (CORS already resolved)
test_cases.given: docker-compose is running with backend and frontend in separate containers, frontend served at http://localhost:5173 and backend at http://localhost:8000
test_cases.when: the frontend calls a protected endpoint (e.g. GET /api/users) with an Authorization: Bearer <token> header
test_cases.then: the CORS preflight succeeds and the request returns 200, not a CORS-rejected or 401/403 response, confirming allow_headers=["*"] already permits Authorization

test_cases.title: Login and authenticated session persist across page refresh under docker-compose
test_cases.given: the app is running via docker-compose up (backend and frontend containers)
test_cases.when: a user logs in through the frontend UI, then refreshes the page
test_cases.then: the user remains authenticated and protected endpoints continue to respond 200 without re-login

test_cases.title: Login and authenticated session behave identically under local dev vs docker-compose
test_cases.given: the app is running via local dev (uvicorn on localhost:8000, npm run dev on localhost:5173)
test_cases.when: a user logs in and refreshes the page
test_cases.then: the login, protected-endpoint access, and refresh-persistence behavior matches the docker-compose case exactly
